title: 2026-10-28_Sofacy_Fysbis_Backdoor_Investigation_d9a
description: Investigate a compromise by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The target network has been compromised by the Sofacy group using the Fysbis backdoor. Your task is to investigate the compromise, identify the malicious activity, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and identify lateral movement to other hosts. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.
levels.local_content: You have SSH access to the `target` host with the username `cyrano` and password `cyrano`. From there, you can investigate the compromised system and identify lateral movement to other hosts. Enter the passkey `start` to proceed.

levels.title: Investigate Suspicious Network Activity
levels.content: Users have reported slow network performance. Investigate the `target` host for any suspicious network activity that could be causing this issue. Submit the port number used for suspicious communication.
levels.solution: Check the network connections and running services on the `target` host. The suspicious port `80` is used for communication.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Network performance issues can often be caused by unusual or unauthorized network connections.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Check the network connections and running services on the `target` host.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `netstat -tuln` to list all network connections and identify the suspicious port.

levels.title: Identify Persistence Mechanism
levels.content: Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot on the `target` host. Submit the systemd service name responsible for the persistence.
levels.solution: Look for systemd services or cron jobs that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service. The systemd service `ksysdefd.service` is responsible for the persistence.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Persistence mechanisms often involve system services or scheduled tasks that ensure malicious software runs automatically.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for systemd services or cron jobs that might be responsible for starting the suspicious service.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `systemctl list-unit-files --type=service` to list all systemd services and identify the suspicious one.

levels.title: Investigate Lateral Movement
levels.content: Check if the attacker has moved laterally from the `target` host to the `next-target` host. Submit the script path used for lateral movement.
levels.solution: Look for any scripts or services that might be transferring files or executing commands remotely. The script `/usr/local/bin/payload-transfer.sh` is used for lateral movement.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Lateral movement often involves scripts or services that transfer files or execute commands on other systems.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Look for any scripts or services that might be transferring files or executing commands remotely.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Use the command `find /usr/local/bin -type f -name '*.sh'` to search for scripts in the `/usr/local/bin` directory.
